doc.title: Vince Lateano interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Leaving at 18 with Carmen Cavallaro; parents' reaction
summary: He took the Cavallaro gig at 18; supportive blue-collar parents warned about the insecurity of music.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And I mean but it was a good gig. It was a demanding gig. I learned a lot and I saw the country.
You were only 18 at the time?
Yeah. I was 18 at the time.
What did your parents think about that?

Well they were very supportive. They were blue collar people. They tried to warn me of the pitfalls and they were right. They said that’s a pretty rough way to make a living. You know, what are you going to do when there’s no work, and so forth, and job security and so forth. And I said I don’t know. And we all go through that. And they were right. And it’s the same. There’s work and there’s no work. But you have to learn to deal with it and it’s not for everybody. You know. You’re a musician.
I do lots of things too you know.
